_doc: THE declared scientific release inventory (2026-08-09 post-response-2 audit, 3.1).
The release manifest used to hash whatever JSON and Parquet files happened to
sit under three result directories -- 185 files. That covered the analysis
summaries and left out the things a reader would actually need to reproduce or
audit them: the 10,928 feature shards the analyses are computed from, the 459
archived voltage traces the waveform gate inspects, every figure, every report,
most of data/provenance, the model source assets, the compiled mechanism
record, and the source tree itself.
This file names each class of release content explicitly. Verification fails
when a class is under-populated, when a listed file has changed, when a file
matching an included pattern is NOT in the manifest, or when the manifest was
built from a different revision than the one checked out. Adding release
content therefore requires adding it here, which is the point: an inventory
that is inferred from whatever is on disk cannot detect an omission.

feature_shards.what: every simulated feature row and its identity sidecar

trace_archives.what: archived voltage traces retained for waveform inspection, with metadata

figures.what: every published figure, in both raster and vector form

provenance.what: downloads, mechanism builds, calibrations, audits, gate evidence inputs

model_assets.what: downloaded published model sources -- morphologies and mechanism code. HASHED HERE, NOT NECESSARILY REDISTRIBUTED: 12 of 14 implementations carry 'ModelDB terms / free for academic use', which grants use to a reader and not redistribution to this project. The deposited archive ships data/provenance/downloads.json (URL + SHA-256 per asset) and tools/fetch_models.py reconstructs the tree from it. See docs/ASSET_REDISTRIBUTION.md

configuration.what: every frozen configuration the campaign and analysis read

source.what: the code that produced everything above

_doc: THE campaign set a release must contain, declared here and nowhere else.
resolve_gate_subjects() used to build this list from the entries in
configs/experiments/campaigns.json that CURRENTLY HAVE FEATURE SHARDS ON
DISK. Two consequences, both found by the 2026-08-09 post-response-3 audit
(P0-4B): deleting a whole campaign directory removed it from the
requirement instead of reporting it missing, and `sobol` -- which is
generated by tools/run_sobol.py and is not an entry in campaigns.json at
all -- was absent from every coverage requirement even though this file
already listed it under waveform_campaigns. Its records happened to exist
and pass; deleting them would not have opened a coverage hole.
A requirement inferred from the artifacts it is meant to check cannot
detect an absence. This list is the requirement; the filesystem is what is
checked against it.
pilot_policy: `pilot` IS a required campaign for D1/D3/REPLAY: it is 50 stored rows that
sit in the release inventory, so it must be re-simulable and replayable.
It is excluded from waveform_campaigns and from every analysis arm, for the
reason stated there: a cost-measurement run for one model that feeds no
endpoint table. Required to exist and be reproducible; not required to

_doc: Gate roll-ups are keyed by gate NAME, so one passing REPLAY record satisfied
the mandatory REPLAY gate no matter which campaign it came from. Coverage is
declared here as named SUBJECTS, resolved against `required_campaigns`
and the model registry at build time, and every one of them must be matched
by a passing record.

primary_models = every model with feature shards MINUS PRIMARY_EXCLUSIONS: the implementations that actually cast a vote. A model excluded on a gate failure is blocked by its own line in `blockers`, not by coverage.

N5 is deliberately absent from this list: it tests rheobase-probe SEMANTICS on a synthetic adapter (tri-state outcome, failure propagation, the non-monotonic ladder), which is model-independent by construction. A per-model coverage requirement for it would demand NEURON runs that duplicate N1 without testing anything N5 is about.
Files that exist, hash consistently, and should not be in the release.
The analyses class accepts results/analyses/**/*.json|parquet, so seven
obsolete *_n4_projected files and the perturbations_fast5* family were
shipped as release outputs. One of them, decision_n4_projected.json, still
asserted an overall H-G conclusion with H-B scored 0/2 -- directly
contradicting the current no-label decision (2026-08-09 post-response-3
audit, P0-4C). The manifest proved those bytes had not changed. It could
not say they should not be there.
An arm name that is no longer in the declared arm registry, or an output
family the current runner does not generate, is an ORPHAN. Verification
fails on any orphan present outside _withdrawn/. Quarantining one is a
deliberate act recorded here, not a silent deletion.

rationale.*_n4_projected*: n4_projected was removed as a duplicate sensitivity arm; the projection now lives in the primary arm's source table
rationale.*fast5*: a five-model fast pass used during development; the current runner does not generate it

_doc: Every campaign whose rows enter a reported analysis must have retained,
reloaded and independently checked voltage traces (2026-08-09 audit, 3.3).
`pilot` is excluded and the reason is stated rather than left implicit:
it is a 50-row cost-measurement run for one model, it feeds no endpoint
table, and gate D1 describes it as such.

excluded.pilot: 50-row cost-measurement run; feeds no endpoint table
